newsitem.title: USA: UAW, Big Three discussing parts outsourcing - NYT.
newsitem.headline: UAW, Big Three discussing parts outsourcing - NYT.

text.p: Detroit's Big Three auto makers and the United Automobile Workers union are discussing a landmark proposal to resolve their dispute over outside sourcing of auto parts, The New York Times reported on Friday.
The proposal was first made by the manufacturers and has been pushed by Ford Motor Co in particular, according to people close to the talks.

The proposal calls for both sides to make broad concessions that they have resisted in the past. The auto makers and the UAW are negotiating to replace their current three-year labour contract, which expires at midnight on Sept 14.
Under the new proposal, each auto maker would agree not to let its unionised work force fall much below current levels for the three or more years that the next contract lasts.

In exchange, the auto makers -- Ford, General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp -- want the union's permission to pay permanently lower wages in any new auto-parts businesses they may enter, the sources said.
The compromise being negotiated is intended to reassure current UAW members that their jobs are secure even if the auto makers buy more parts from outside vendors.
